The premise really enticed me. A football (soccer) game with fights akin to that of Tekken/Street Fighter. On paper it sounds pretty ridiculous, but potentially like a lot of fun. 

First off, the menu screen had a cheap but endearing polish to it. It seemed like all of the representative teams (based on countries) along with everything else set out on the menu, was voiced by the same guy. I didn't mind that because this is an independent product.

When I got stuck into the gameplay, my opinion swayed very quickly, and that endearment turned into unadulterated rage (no pun intended). 

Every function within the context of the game feels delayed. For example, shots and passes feel like they take a good second before they're activated. That amount of latency makes the game almost unplayable. 

The fighting sections, which proceed a bad tackle or 'red card' scenario, are much the same. Janky, delayed controls which don't respond quickly enough, along with poor animations and pre-ps2 era graphics make this game absolutely unplayable. 

I really can't recommend this. I took a chance on Soccer Rage despite it's early access status, and it really didn't deliver on any of its promises in any way whatsoever. 

The naive child inside me is saying "Maybe it'll get better. Give it time. What if it's just having a rough start? Who knows, it could be as successful as Rocket League one day!".

All hope is dead. Just stick to Rocket League everyone.

This game is a fighting/soccer hybrid with robots. It's clearly early access as most of the content is locked. Here's my objective opinion for whatever it's worth: 

The potential is high in this one. The gameplay is relatively simplistic but very addictive. You can have 5 v 5, 7 v 7, and 11 v 11 soccer matches. The desired goal is the same as soccer, however the twist is your robots will go into "Rage" and you can start a fight, potentially disabling apponent's players. 

The combat is actually a fun little diversion, and is well done considering the game is not a pure fighting game. There are combos and the controls aren't too stiff in combat. You have 4 different attack buttons, can jump, duck, and attack with fair fluidity. It's a timed battle. If you completely disable an apponent, they'll "break" and will be disabled for the soccer portion of the game. If no ones health fully expires in combat before time is up, the fight is over and you continue. 

The soccer portion of the game is done pretty well. The passing and "shooting" is accurate, you can pick up speed with a run button, and if you kick the ball hard enough you can damage the goalie over time. You have slides and trips and can switch players on the fly. The controls are a little complex considering how simple the gameplay is, but once you get used to it, the gameplay is very addictive. Additionally, the "sci-fi" art style is a lot of fun.

There are some definite improvements that need to be made, though. As I mentioned at the top, most of the customization and features are locked out, though there are place-holders for the content, giving you a good idea as to the future goals of the developers. Switching to the soccer player closest to the ball can be a bit buggy and fighting combat against the AI on normal can be frustrating. Sometimes they'll lock you into a juggle until almost all of your health is gone. Despite a run button, the game feels a little "slow" as well, but the benefit to this is that you really have to pass a few times to push the ball up the field, meaning you can't just take off with the ball, run ahead of all of the AI and take your shot. You have to be more strategic. 

All in all, it's a fun game, which would be made more fun with some friends to play with. The potential for the kind of fun you'd get out of a game like Rocket League is here, though the game isn't nearly as polished as Rocket League in it's current state. If the developers really want to take the time to develope Soccer Rage into a great "under the radar" gem, the foundation is there. Beyond that, you just don't see many games like this. It's refreshing to see a developer attempt to make something so bold.

Esta fue la gota que derramo el vaso, no vuelvo a apoyar un indie dentro del periodo early access, a menos de que se vuelvan muy populares o esten estúpidamente baratos (o me lo embarren en un bundle), ¿porque? simple:

Las pseúdo desarrolladoras indies o personas que lanzan su juego se van por el mundo pregonando una idea o un concepto que pueden "según ellos" llevar a la realidad. Ok. La gente les apoya, compra sus juegos incompletos, apoya en el feedback, cuando te das cuenta, el resultado final es mierda; básicamente pagaste por mierda. 

[h1]Ejemplo #1 Air Brawl / Landfall Games[/h1]

Hacen un juego, lo promocionan, LO VENDEN, la gente lo compra y que deciden al final, darlo gratis porque no pueden con el proyecto... ("porque no hay gente jugando" se dicen ellos), tu dinero se fue al caño...

[h1]Ejemplo #2 Pool Nation FX / Cherry Pop Games[/h1]

Hacen un juego, lo promocionan, LO VENDEN, la gente lo compra y que deciden al final, darlo gratis porque no pueden con el proyecto... ("porque no hay gente jugando" se dicen ellos), regalando basura de single player para quien ya lo compro...

[h1]Ejemplo #3 Soccer Rage / Stamina-Games[/h1]

Hacen un juego, lo promocionan, LO VENDEN, la gente lo compra y que deciden al final, darlo gratis a manera de llaves en cualquier lado porque no pueden con el proyecto... ("porque no hay gente jugando" se dicen ellos), dejando el juego en un status injugable y olvidado para siempre, tu dinero se fue al caño...

[h1]Ejemplo #4 ♥♥♥ MANDO / UNDEAD[/h1]

Por muchas cosas, el caso que menos me ha decepcionado, tampoco es que es me tenga muy feliz; el juego aún esta incompleto, solo hubo una update y se acabó, lo demás es historia...

[b]Como estos, muchos...[/b]
Por experiencia propia, sé que no es sencillo, sé que no es fácil, sé que no es productivo; pero si lo van a hacer haganlo bien! No cobren por algo que no van a terminar o piensan en abandonar, denlo gratis en las versiones tempranas y cuando cobren fuerza, vendanlo! O simplemente no publiquen porquerías inconclusas, sean objetivos.

¿Porque hago este analisis? Porque veo que a todos los desarrolladores les importa una mierda lo que los usuarios pagaron alguna vez, me incluyo, normalmente no acepto regalos de desarrolladores indie que conozco personalmente, los apoyo pagando por sus "juegos" el resultado es decepcionante...

Nota: Mi análisis lo hago desde el punto de vista del consumidor, no soy desarrollador (de videojuegos), pero sin consumo no hay nada. Si te gusta mi análisis bien! Sino realmente no me quita el sueño lo que pienses de esto, así que ahorrate tus lágrimas de cocodrilo comentando insultos...

PV中にもある格ゲーめいた乱闘は、何度か削り合いしてるとランダム？にサッカーから格ゲーに移行するようです（なので試合展開によっては乱闘が全くないこともしばしば）。ただ体力がない状態で削られるとそもそも乱闘に移行せずに死んだりするんで気をつけましょう。
格ゲー部分についてはレバー＋攻撃4ボタンのオーソドックスさを感じさせる作りですが、攻撃ボタンのレスポンスが悪い感じがするので先行入力気味にきっちり入力していく必要があるかと思います。コツを掴まないとやられっぱなしでストレスがたまるかもしれません（コツを掴めるほど頻繁には乱闘起きないけど……）。
立ち大Kヒットからは距離がよほど離れていなければサマソ（→大K）が繋がり、外すとでかい隙があるものの入ればそのままジャンプ攻撃に繋げられるので、狙える状況なら積極的に狙っていきたい。
数回触った感じ、ヒット状況によっては立ち大K→サマソ→空コン→着地立ち大K……とコンボを伸ばせそうです。とはいえ現時点ではトレモがないのと乱闘に入る確定状況が不明なので細かいところはわかりません。

ところで選手が破壊された時に「メディーック！」って声が聞こえますが、死んだ後ボディパーツが元のポジションにひっそり置いてある状態です。……治療はちゃんとしてるんですかね？ｗ
破壊された選手は終了までそのままなので、当たり前ですができるだけ倒されないようにしましょう。まあ3人位いなくても立ち回り次第で充分勝てますが。個人的に感じたところ、日本チームのCPUは格ゲー部分の立ち回りが比較的強い気がします。慣れるまで相手にするのはやめといたほうがいいかもしれません（あくまで体感ですが……）。

以上とりとめなく雑記めいた感じですが、安いし気軽に遊べるし、このままクオリティアップしていけば良ゲーくらいにはなるんじゃないかと思います。
未実装の部分もいっぱいあるようなので、今後に期待しています。

Soccer Rage sounds like a fun game, a mixture between a fighting game and FIFA soccer that I played with.

While the game is in beta, I wanted to do a beta preview, not the actual review of the game in whole since it is not complete.  As it is Early Access, the game does have a great amount of potential.  Here are the following pros and cons:

Pros
-Soccer!  What more could you ask for?
-National teams for countries to play with
-Fighting implemented like in NHL where you must duke it out between both players.
-Unique animations in the fighting styles
-Unique uniforms for both Local and Away teams

Cons
-Early Access
-Barebones as it is
-Clipping of certain scenes are found
-Jerky, unreliable response using gamepad controls.

Special notes for Game Developer:

Using the button to exit out of Replay and Kickoff results in both Replay and Kickoff text to appear at the same time.

When I enter into fight mode, the AI continues to fight me even if I am not prepared.  While executing my controls before the screen shows two players fighting, my player keeps on fighting without me knowing about it.  There's no proper executing of the fight scene before it begins.  Holding the AI and player from fighting until the words announced, "Fight!" ends should help.

The AI opposing team is too fast, and are capable of playing the ball against a newcomer to this game.  Slowing them down, or potentially beefing up the player 1's AI along with the goalie would help.  The goalie would not defend the post after a few rounds.  After my goalie entered into a Rage fight with someone and won, he refused to defend the post.  He would stand there and then receive hit after hit with the ball.  So amazing he can survive such encounters!

Whenever I switch to a new player on my team, I noticed that the previous player I selected stops.  It just stands there for a few seconds before rushing to move into its position.  If I select the one player repeatedly, the player can't move for a second or more.  It results in a loss of the ball, loss of movement, and unable to defend aggressively.

These are mostly some of the reasons why I lost my first Quickmatch as Germany against Japan!  0-8...  *shudders*...  Not ever doing that again.  :P  They're a World Cup winner in 2014!  Not World Cup losers, haha.
lol The idea is great! It so fun to have a new approach on Soccer. It reminds me Mutant League, but with real fighting. Can't wait to see the final product.
